about: Hand-written rotation guides for the mage's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: Frost in a raid is a **Frostbolt** caster that cashes in two procs: free **Arcane Missiles** from **Missile Barrage** and instant **Ice Lance** casts on **Fingers of Frost**. One **Fire Blast** in the last seconds of the fight uses time no **Frostbolt** can fill.
why: **Arcane Missiles** on **Missile Barrage** comes first. Each **Frostbolt** that lands has a 20% chance to make your next Missiles free and twice as fast (the full damage in 2.5 seconds), and they are about a fifth of your damage in the simulator.

**Ice Lance** on **Fingers of Frost** comes next. Each **Frostbolt** chill has a 15% chance to treat your next 2 spells as if the target were frozen; a frozen target takes 300% more damage from **Ice Lance** and **Shatter** adds 50% crit chance, so spend both charges on **Ice Lance**. With both procs up, the simulator measured the free Missiles first slightly better (0.2%).

**Frostbolt** fills everything else: 2.5 seconds with **Improved Frostbolt**, and the spell that rolls for both procs. **Winter's Chill** needs no button: in Forever it is your own debuff, each Frost hit adds a stack (+2% crit to your **Frostbolt** and **Ice Lance**, up to 5), and steady casting keeps it full.

**Fire Blast** waits for the last 3 seconds. A **Frostbolt** started then would still be casting or in flight when the boss dies, while **Fire Blast** is instant; the simulator measured this 0.5% better. The rotation search kept it out of the rest of the fight: no Frost talent improves it, it costs more mana than a **Frostbolt** (340 against 290) and it rolls for neither proc.
**Presence of Mind** at the pull makes your next spell instant. Its cooldown is 3 minutes, so a 3-minute fight gets one; in a longer fight press it again when it is back.

Mana: the list uses your mana gem (from **Conjure Mana Ruby**) as soon as you are down to 80% mana, and **Evocation** only below 20% mana with more than 25 seconds left. With a raid's mana buffs the simulator never needed **Evocation** in a 3-minute fight.
caveats: Several targets: this list is for one boss, and the simulator's raid fights are single-target. For packs, **Blizzard**, **Cone of Cold** and **Arcane Explosion** are your area spells.
Moving: **Frostbolt** needs you to stand still. **Ice Lance** and **Fire Blast** are instant, and **Presence of Mind** makes one **Frostbolt** instant.
Threat: the simulator ignores it. On a fresh pull, give the tank a few seconds before your opener.
diverge: In the last 3 seconds, cast **Fire Blast** instead of starting a **Frostbolt** (the Advanced line above).
Without a paladin's or shaman's mana buffs you run dry sooner: below 20% mana with more than 25 seconds to go, channel **Evocation**. Any later and the mana comes back too late to spend.
If you must move while **Fingers of Frost** is up, spend the charges on **Ice Lance** as you go: it is instant.

leveling.plan: Frost levels by slowing, freezing and shattering: **Frostbolt** slows the mob as it walks in, **Frost Nova** freezes it when it arrives, and you step back and **Ice Lance** the frozen target. In the fight lab at level 60, **Ice Lance** is about 58% of this build's damage, **Frostbolt** 29% and **Fire Blast** 11%.
why: **Frostbolt** from as far away as you can and whenever nothing else applies: its 40% slow buys extra casts before the mob reaches you, and every chill can freeze it (**Frostbite**, 15%) or light up **Fingers of Frost** (15%: your next 2 spells count as cast on a frozen target). If the mob would reach you before the cast ends, **Fire Blast** it instead, or wand it while it closes if **Fire Blast** is on cooldown and **Frost Nova** is ready.

**Frost Nova** when it reaches you, then step back out of melee: it roots the mob, and once you are out of reach it cannot hit you or push back your casts. **Improved Frost Nova** (levels 55-56) brings it back 4 seconds sooner.

**Ice Lance** while the mob is frozen (**Frost Nova**, a **Frostbite** freeze or a **Fingers of Frost** charge): 200% more damage to a frozen target, 50% more crit chance from **Shatter** and bigger crits from **Ice Shards**. It is instant, so cast it again and again while the freeze lasts. In the fight lab a kill at level 60 takes about 5.6 seconds longer without **Ice Lance**, 4.2 without **Shatter** and 2.4 without **Ice Shards**.

**Fire Blast** is the instant for the moments a **Frostbolt** does not fit: the mob about to reach you, the mob on you with **Frost Nova** down, or a kill it will finish. **Incineration** (levels 50-52) adds 6% crit chance to it and to **Ice Lance**.

Finishing: the tuned rules (2026-10-22) start no **Frostbolt** once the mob is below a fifth of its health and no **Fire Blast** below a tenth; an **Ice Lance** that will kill, or the wand, finishes it.

The Arcane points (levels 32-49) are for mana: **Arcane Concentration** makes a damage spell free now and then (10% per hit) and **Arcane Meditation** keeps half your mana regeneration going while you cast; in the fight lab each is worth about a second per kill at level 60.
**Counterspell** (level 24) a mob that casts spells: it stops the cast and locks that school for 10 seconds.
caveats: This build takes neither **Cold Snap** nor **Ice Barrier**: skip the list's lines for them. The hand-made build under Other builds has both (**Cold Snap** at 37, **Ice Barrier** at 40).
**Cone of Cold** stays out of single pulls: the tuned rules never cast it (about 2% faster kills in the fight lab). **Winter's Chill**, the build's last point, only helps **Cone of Cold**.
Drink below a third of your mana; **Evocation** is for between fights, whenever it is ready and you are under 40% mana.
**Frost Armor** and **Ice Armor** can chill a mob that hits you, another roll for **Frostbite** to freeze it.
Pulls of several mobs are a different game: the AoE build under Other builds gathers about four mobs, freezes them with **Frost Nova** and uses **Blizzard** and **Cone of Cold**.
diverge: If **Frost Nova** is on cooldown when the mob arrives, **Fire Blast** it and keep casting; a build with **Cold Snap** resets Nova instead when it has more than 8 seconds left and the mob still has 40% of its health.
Low on mana in a fight: let an **Ice Lance** into the freeze or the wand finish a nearly dead mob rather than start a **Frostbolt**.

raid.plan: This hybrid plays exactly like the Frost page: **Frostbolt** as the filler, free **Arcane Missiles** on **Missile Barrage**, **Ice Lance** on **Fingers of Frost**, and **Fire Blast** only at the very end. Its Arcane points add hit and crit to the Missiles, free spells, Intellect and damage; the build on this page takes neither **Arcane Power** nor **Presence of Mind**.
why: **Arcane Missiles** on **Missile Barrage** comes first. Each **Frostbolt** that lands has a 20% chance to make your next Missiles free and twice as fast (the full damage in 2.5 seconds); **Arcane Focus** and **Arcane Impact** add hit and crit to them.

**Ice Lance** on **Fingers of Frost** comes next. Each **Frostbolt** chill has a 15% chance to treat your next 2 spells as if the target were frozen; **Ice Lance** deals 300% more damage to a frozen target and **Shatter** adds 50% crit chance, so both charges go to **Ice Lance**. With both procs up, the simulator measured the free Missiles first slightly better (0.2%).

**Frostbolt** fills everything else and is the spell that rolls for both procs. **Winter's Chill**, if your build takes it, is passive: each Frost hit adds a stack of +2% crit to your **Frostbolt** and **Ice Lance**, one stack per talent point.

**Fire Blast** waits for the last 3 seconds, when a **Frostbolt** could no longer land before the boss dies; the simulator measured this 0.5% better. The rotation search kept it out of the rest of the fight: no damage talent here improves it, it costs more mana and it rolls for neither proc.

**Arcane Concentration** (3 points) gives each damage spell a 6% chance to make the next one free. **Arcane Mind** adds 10% Intellect and doubles the crit bonus of your Arcane spells (the Missiles), and **Arcane Instability** adds 3% damage and 3% crit to every spell. There is no cooldown to press at the pull besides trinkets and a potion.
Mana: your mana gem (from **Conjure Mana Ruby**) goes at 80% mana and **Evocation** only below 20% mana with more than 25 seconds left; in a full raid the simulator never needed **Evocation**.
caveats: The Frost page plays the same list with more Frost points; the simulator puts the two pages within 2% of each other, a tie.
Several targets: this list is for one boss. For packs, **Blizzard**, **Cone of Cold** and **Arcane Explosion** are your area spells.
Moving: **Ice Lance** and **Fire Blast** are instant. Threat is not in the simulator: give the tank a few seconds on a fresh pull.
diverge: In the last 3 seconds, cast **Fire Blast** instead of starting a **Frostbolt**.
Without raid mana buffs, channel **Evocation** below 20% mana while more than 25 seconds remain; later than that, the mana comes back too late to spend.

leveling.plan: This hybrid plays the Frost list with one Arcane addition: **Frostbolt** at range, **Frost Nova** and a step back when the mob arrives, **Ice Lance** into the freeze, and a free, fast **Arcane Missiles** whenever **Missile Barrage** lights up. Its first 25 points (levels 10-34) are Frost; **Missile Barrage** comes at 35-36 and the rest of the Arcane half from 43. In the fight lab at level 60, **Ice Lance** is about 53% of its damage, **Frostbolt** 26%, **Fire Blast** 10% and **Arcane Missiles** 9%.
why: **Frostbolt** from as far away as you can and as the filler: its slow buys casts before the mob arrives, its chill rolls **Frostbite** (15% to freeze) and **Fingers of Frost** (15%: the next 2 spells count as cast on a frozen target), and with **Missile Barrage** (levels 35-36) each one has a 20% chance to light it up. **Improved Frostbolt** (levels 10-14) cuts its cast by half a second.

**Arcane Missiles** only on a **Missile Barrage** proc: the channel is half as long and costs nothing. Cast it at range or into a freeze, not while the mob is hitting you: **Improved Channeling** (2 points) gives only a 40% chance that a hit does not interrupt it. The fight lab casts it about once every three kills at level 60.

**Frost Nova** when the mob reaches you, then step back; **Ice Lance** while it is frozen: 200% more damage to a frozen target, 50% more crit chance from **Shatter** and bigger crits from **Ice Shards**. In the fight lab a kill at level 60 takes about 3.7 seconds longer without **Shatter**, 2.9 without **Ice Lance** and 1.3 without **Missile Barrage**.

**Fire Blast** when the mob would reach you before a **Frostbolt** lands, when it is on you and **Frost Nova** is down, and to finish one it will kill. The tuned rules (2026-10-23) start no **Frostbolt** or **Fire Blast** once the mob is below a tenth of its health: an **Ice Lance** that will kill, or the wand, finishes it.

**Arcane Blast** (level 54) is one of the points that open **Arcane Meditation**'s row; this list never casts it. **Arcane Concentration** (levels 46-50) and **Arcane Meditation** (56-58) are for mana.
caveats: This build takes no **Cold Snap**: skip that part of the list. Before level 35 it is a plain Frost mage, with no **Missile Barrage** yet.
**Cone of Cold** stays out of single pulls: the tuned rules never cast it (about 1% faster kills in the fight lab). **Winter's Chill** (level 42) only helps **Cone of Cold**.

Rest: the tuned rules drink below 15% of your mana and eat below 40% of your health, later than the other mage lists (each a little faster per kill in the fight lab); **Evocation** between fights when it is ready and you are under 40% mana.
diverge: On a nearly dead mob, skip even a free **Arcane Missiles** (the fight lab does not channel it into a mob a few wand hits from death): an **Ice Lance** or **Fire Blast** that will kill, or the wand.
Mob on you with **Frost Nova** down: **Fire Blast**, then keep casting **Frostbolt**; the list does not use **Cone of Cold** here.

raid.plan: Arcane in a raid builds **Arcane Blast** stacks and spends them. Each **Arcane Blast** makes your next other spell stronger and the next **Arcane Blast** much dearer, so free **Arcane Missiles** from **Missile Barrage** and a **Fire Blast** every 6 seconds spend the stacks before the cost runs away.
why: **Arcane Blast** is the filler: a 2.5-second cast that adds a stack each time (up to 4, for 8 seconds). Each stack adds 10% to the damage of your other spells (15% to **Arcane Missiles**, fitted to beta logs) and 175% to the next **Arcane Blast**'s mana cost; casting any other damage spell spends them all.

**Arcane Missiles** on **Missile Barrage** comes first. Each **Arcane Blast** that lands has a 40% chance to make your next Missiles free and twice as fast, and the Missiles spend your stacks at 15% each: about a third of your damage in the simulator.

**Fire Blast** whenever it is ready is why this Arcane build spends 11 points in Fire: **Improved Fire Blast** brings it back every 6 seconds and **Incineration** adds crit. It is instant, it takes your stacks' bonus, and it puts **Arcane Blast** back to its base cost. Adding it was the biggest gain of the rotation search, about 8% over three steps.

**Arcane Power** and **Presence of Mind** go at the pull: 30% more damage for 15 seconds (at 30% more mana cost) and one instant spell. Both have 3-minute cooldowns, so a 3-minute fight gets one of each.
Mana: **Evocation** only below 15% mana with more than 20 seconds left. With a raid's mana buffs, your mana gems and a mana potion, the simulator almost never needed it.
caveats: Without a raid's mana buffs you run dry sooner. The simulator's list for playing without them also spends two stacks on a **Frostbolt** when **Fire Blast** is not ready, which keeps **Arcane Blast** cheap.
Moving: **Arcane Blast** and **Arcane Missiles** both need you to stand. **Fire Blast** is your instant, and **Presence of Mind** makes one **Arcane Blast** instant.
Threat: **Arcane Subtlety** cuts your Arcane threat by 30%, but the simulator ignores threat, and **Arcane Power** at the pull is when you are most likely to pull the boss.
Several targets: this list is for one boss. **Arcane Explosion** hits everything within 10 yards.
diverge: In the last 40 seconds, stop resetting with **Fire Blast** and keep casting **Arcane Blast**. Its cost climbs, but mana left when the boss dies is wasted and your free Missiles spend bigger stacks; the simulator measured these end-of-fight rules about 1% better together.
In the last 3 seconds an **Arcane Blast** cannot finish: cast the **Fire Blast** you saved.
In a fight longer than 3 minutes, use **Arcane Power** and **Presence of Mind** again when they are back, and channel **Evocation** below 15% mana while more than 20 seconds remain.

leveling.plan: Arcane levels on its own spells: **Arcane Wrath** to open, two **Arcane Blast** stacks while the mob walks in, then **Arcane Missiles**, which you keep channeling when the mob reaches you; the tuned rules (2026-10-22) never cast **Frost Nova**. In the fight lab at level 60, **Arcane Missiles** is about 71% of this build's damage, **Arcane Blast** 16%, **Fire Blast** 7% and **Arcane Wrath** 5%.
why: **Presence of Mind** (level 30) at the pull makes your first cast instant (in the fight lab the opening **Arcane Wrath**); **Arcane Power** (level 40) at the pull too while you have more than half your mana: 30% more damage and 30% more mana cost for 15 seconds.

**Arcane Wrath** (level 25) opens when its 3.5-second cast lands before the mob arrives, then goes out whenever it is ready (6-second cooldown) and the cast fits. It gains spell damage equal to 5% of your maximum mana.

**Arcane Blast** (level 20) twice while the mob walks in: each cast gives all your spells spell damage (15% of your Intellect) for 15 seconds and makes the next **Arcane Blast** 175% more expensive, so the fight lab stops at two, and starts one only while it costs at most a quarter of your mana and will finish before the mob reaches you. Without it a kill at level 60 takes about 4.1 seconds longer in the fight lab.

**Arcane Missiles** is the main spell, at range and in melee: **Improved Channeling** at 5/5 (done at level 31) gives a 100% chance that hits do not interrupt the channel. **Missile Barrage** (levels 10-11; 40% from **Arcane Blast**, 20% from **Arcane Wrath**) makes the next one free and twice as fast: cast it at once after your two stacks, or when the mob is on you. Without **Missile Barrage** a kill at level 60 takes about 4.3 seconds longer, without **Improved Channeling** 2.9.
No **Frost Nova**: the tuned rules measured kills about 2% faster without it. Our reading: with hits unable to stop the Missiles, the global cooldown and the step back cost more than the hits do.

When the mob is on you and below a fifth of its health, **Cone of Cold** and a step back (a tuned rule, about 1.5% faster); **Fire Blast** finishes a mob it will kill. The Fire half (levels 44-60) is mostly for **Fire Blast**: **Improved Fire Blast** takes 2 seconds off its cooldown, **Incineration** adds 6% crit chance, **Impact** gives your Fire spells a 10% chance to stun for 2 seconds. **Improved Fireball** and **Pyroblast** only open the rows to **Master of Elements**: the list casts neither **Fireball** nor **Pyroblast**.
caveats: This build has no **Ice Lance**: skip that line of the list.

Mana: **Arcane Missiles** costs 655 at top rank, every **Arcane Blast** stack makes the next one dearer and **Arcane Power** adds 30%. **Frostbolt** (290 at top rank) is for when you cannot afford the Missiles. Drink below a third of your mana and use **Evocation** between fights when it is ready and you are under 40% mana.
The tuned rules eat below 40% of your health, not two thirds: the fight lab measured kills slightly faster that way, with no deaths in its tuning runs.
The fight lab measured only single pulls for this list: with several mobs on you, **Frost Nova** and **Arcane Explosion** (everything within 10 yards) are back in play.
diverge: If the mob would reach you before an **Arcane Blast** or **Arcane Wrath** finishes, do not start it: channel **Arcane Missiles** instead (an instant cast with **Presence of Mind** is the exception).
A mob that hits harder than a normal same-level mob is still worth a **Frost Nova**: the rule only says it costs time against the mobs the fight lab models.
Against a caster mob, **Counterspell** it when it starts a cast, as every mage list in the fight lab does.

raid.plan: Fire keeps its own **Improved Scorch** debuff at 5 stacks, fires **Fire Blast** on cooldown and casts **Fireball** in between. Crits build **Heating Up**; at 3 stacks **Pyroblast** becomes a 1.5-second cast.
why: **Fire Blast** first whenever it is ready: every 6 seconds with **Improved Fire Blast**, instant, and **Incineration** and **Critical Mass** make it crit often, feeding **Heating Up** and **Ignite**. The simulator measured using it on cooldown, with no mana saving, 3.7% better than the rule it replaced.

**Scorch** keeps Fire Vulnerability at 5 stacks. In Forever **Improved Scorch** is your own debuff: +3% to your Fire damage per stack, for 30 seconds. Build 5 stacks, then refresh it once 7.5 seconds or less are left so a long cast cannot let it drop; the list shows only the stack count, but the early refresh is part of the rule (the simulator measured 7.5 seconds 0.4% better than 5).

**Pyroblast** waits for 3 stacks of **Heating Up**. Each crit from **Fireball**, **Fire Blast** or **Scorch** takes 25% off your next **Pyroblast**'s 6-second cast, so 3 stacks make it 1.5 seconds: your biggest hit for its cast time. The list's 2-stack line is a last-chance rule: cast a 3-second **Pyroblast** at 2 stacks only if **Heating Up** has under 3.5 seconds left or the boss dies within 6 seconds.

**Fireball** fills everything else: 3 seconds with **Improved Fireball**, about half your damage, and each crit also starts **Ignite**. The list stops starting it with under 3 seconds left, when it would land too late.

**Combustion** at the pull and whenever it is back (3 minutes): each Fire hit adds 10% crit until you land 3 crits, which fills **Heating Up** fast. It shares its cooldown with **Presence of Mind** (client data), so a build with both gets only one of the two every 3 minutes.
caveats: Mana: Fire runs short even in a full raid. The simulator uses your mana gem (from **Conjure Mana Ruby**) at 80% mana and a mana potion whenever it is ready, and still runs dry now and then; **Master of Elements** refunds 30% of a spell's base cost on each crit.

The raid list has no **Evocation**: in a 3-minute fight with raid buffs the simulator measured it slightly better without (0.2%). In a longer fight or without mana buffs, channel it when nearly empty with plenty of fight left; the simulator's list for playing without raid buffs does so below 10% mana with more than 25 seconds to go.
Several targets: the simulator's own Fire list adds **Blast Wave** and **Flamestrike** at 3 or more targets; this build has no **Blast Wave**, so use **Flamestrike**.
The simulator's boss resists nothing. Against an enemy that resists or ignores Fire, every spell here loses damage, and **Frostbolt** is your fallback.
diverge: In the last 3 seconds a **Fireball** would land too late: cast **Scorch**. The simulator's list uses Rank 1 there, the same line it falls back on when you cannot afford a **Fireball**; Forever gives ranks that low only part of your spell power and fewer talent procs, so use your top **Scorch** whenever you have the 150 mana.
With 2 stacks of **Heating Up** and the boss dying within 6 seconds, cast **Pyroblast** now: the third crit may never come.

leveling.plan: Fire levels with **Fireball** at range and **Fire Blast** up close, and borrows the Frost tree's freeze: **Frost Nova**, step back, and **Ice Lance** the frozen mob; from level 45, **Heating Up** makes some **Pyroblast** casts fast. In the fight lab at level 60, **Ice Lance** is about 34% of this build's damage, **Fire Blast** 24%, **Fireball** 16% and **Pyroblast** 12%.
why: The first 20 points (levels 10-29) are Frost: **Ice Lance** (20), **Shatter** (25-27), **Ice Shards** and **Elemental Precision**. A frozen mob takes 200% more damage from **Ice Lance**, with 50% more crit chance; in the fight lab a kill at level 60 takes about 4.3 seconds longer without **Ice Lance** and 2.8 without **Shatter**. This build has no **Frostbite** or **Fingers of Frost**, so the freeze is **Frost Nova** (back 4 seconds sooner with **Improved Frost Nova**, levels 15-16).

**Fireball** from as far away as you can, and as the filler whenever nothing else applies, while the mob has more than 35% of its health. Below that the tuned rules (2026-10-22) start no **Fireball** or **Scorch** (each about 1% faster): a long cast overkills.

**Fire Blast** is your instant: when the mob would reach you before a **Fireball** lands, when it is on you and **Frost Nova** is down, and to finish a mob it will kill. **Improved Fire Blast** (levels 30-31) takes 2 seconds off its 8-second cooldown.

**Heating Up** (level 45; **Pyroblast** at 44): non-periodic crits with **Fireball**, **Fire Blast** and **Scorch**, and every **Fire Blast** that deals damage, each cut your next **Pyroblast**'s cast by 25%, up to 3 stacks. At 3 stacks its 6-second cast takes 1.5 seconds: cast it then, never without them.
**Frost Nova** when the mob reaches you, then step back; **Ice Lance** while it is frozen.

**Scorch** when the mob is on you and your control is down, above 35% of its health: its 1.5-second cast is pushed back less than a **Fireball**. It also covers the walk-in when **Fire Blast** is on cooldown and a **Fireball** would not land in time.
**Combustion** (level 60) goes at the pull.
caveats: This build takes no **Blast Wave**: skip that line of the list. Before level 44 it has no **Pyroblast** either.

Mana: **Fireball** costs 410 at top rank against 290 for a **Frostbolt**; **Master of Elements** (levels 47-49) refunds 30% of a spell's base cost on each Fire or Frost crit (about 1.3 seconds per kill at level 60 in the fight lab). Drink below a third of your mana and use **Evocation** between fights when it is ready and you are under 40% mana.
**Burning Soul** (levels 41-43) keeps 70% of your Fire casts from being pushed back when a mob reaches you.
Pulls of several mobs: **Flamestrike** hits them all, but the fight lab only measured single pulls for Fire.
diverge: On a nearly dead mob (below about a third), finish with an instant that will kill (**Fire Blast**, an **Ice Lance**) or the wand rather than start a **Fireball** or **Scorch**.

If you run low on mana in a fight, keep **Fire Blast** and **Ice Lance** for the freeze and let the wand finish; the fight lab's list has no mana limit of its own and drinks below a third between fights.

raid.plan: Frostfire is a Fire mage whose main spell is **Frostfire Bolt**: it counts as both Fire and Frost damage, so both trees' talents apply, and its chill lights up **Fingers of Frost** for **Ice Lance**. The Fire side adds **Fire Blast**, **Scorch** upkeep and **Pyroblast** at full **Heating Up**.
why: **Ice Lance** on **Fingers of Frost** comes first. Each **Frostfire Bolt** chill has a 15% chance to treat your next 2 spells as if the target were frozen; a frozen target takes 300% more damage from **Ice Lance** and **Shatter** adds 50% crit, so spend both charges on **Ice Lance**.

**Pyroblast** at 3 stacks of **Heating Up**: crits from **Frostfire Bolt**, **Fire Blast** and **Scorch** each take 25% off its 6-second cast, so 3 stacks make it 1.5 seconds. Unlike the Fire list, this one never casts it at 2 stacks; the simulator measured dropping that line 0.3% better.

**Fire Blast** on cooldown (every 8 seconds: this build has no **Improved Fire Blast**): instant, and its crits feed **Heating Up** and **Ignite**. Using it without a mana condition was the biggest single gain of the full-raid rotation search, about 5%.

**Scorch** keeps Fire Vulnerability (from **Improved Scorch**) at 5 stacks, +15% to your Fire damage, and **Frostfire Bolt** counts as Fire. This list refreshes it once 15 seconds or less of its 30 are left, a wider margin than the Fire list's 7.5.

**Frostfire Bolt** is the main spell: 2.5 seconds with **Improved Fireball**, and one cast rolls for **Fingers of Frost**, **Heating Up** and **Ignite** at once. Below 30% mana the full rotation casts Rank 2 (285 mana against 370): the page's line "when your mana is below 30%". The simulator measured this about 2% better than the old rule of stopping at 10% mana.

**Fireball** (Rank 2 in the full rotation) is last: a stopgap for when you cannot afford even a Rank 2 **Frostfire Bolt**. Forever gives ranks that far below your level only part of your spell power; keep your mana up with gems and a potion so it rarely comes up.
caveats: **Fingers of Frost** charges go to the next 2 spells you cast, whatever they are: do not let a **Frostfire Bolt** use one up.

Mana: **Frostfire Bolt** costs 370 at top rank. The list uses both of your mana gems (from **Conjure Mana Ruby** and **Conjure Mana Citrine**), **Master of Elements** refunds 30% of the base cost on each Fire or Frost crit, and below 30% mana the cheaper Rank 2 stretches what is left.
Moving: **Ice Lance** and **Fire Blast** are instant. For packs, **Flamestrike** and **Blizzard** are your area spells.
**Frostfire Bolt** is new in Forever: its numbers here are the simulator's model of the beta tooltip, not yet checked in game.
The full rotation also opens with **Arcane Power** for builds that take it; this build does not, so skip it.
diverge: Below 30% mana, switch to Rank 2 **Frostfire Bolt** rather than stop casting it; a **Fireball** is a weak stopgap only for when even that is out of reach.

Against a target that resists Fire, **Frostfire Bolt** keeps working (it is checked against the lower of the target's Fire and Frost resistance), while **Fire Blast**, **Scorch** and **Pyroblast** lose damage.

leveling.plan: The Frostfire leveling build is a Frost mage whose bolt changes at level 40: **Frostbolt** before, **Frostfire Bolt** after, with **Frost Nova**, a step back and **Ice Lance** into the freeze throughout. In the fight lab at level 60, **Ice Lance** is about 60% of its damage and **Frostfire Bolt** about 31% (its burn included).
why: **Frostfire Bolt** (trained at level 40) counts as Frost and Fire, so both trees' talents apply, and it slows like **Frostbolt** (40%), so its chill rolls **Frostbite** (15% to freeze) and **Fingers of Frost** (15%: your next 2 spells count as cast on a frozen target). **Improved Fireball** (levels 36-40) cuts its 3-second cast to 2.5. The tuned rules (2026-10-22) cast it down to a tenth of the mob's health.
Before level 40, **Frostbolt** does the same job, but only while the mob has more than 35% of its health; below that, an **Ice Lance** into a freeze or the wand.

**Ice Lance** (level 20) and **Shatter** (25-27) are the build's two most valuable talents in the fight lab at level 60 (without either a kill takes about 7 seconds longer): a frozen mob takes 200% more damage from **Ice Lance**, with 50% more crit chance and **Ice Shards**' bigger crits.
**Frost Nova** when the mob reaches you, then step back out of melee.
**Fire Blast** is a small part here (about 3% of the damage): the tuned rules cast it only while the mob is between a tenth and a fifth of its health and you have more than 30% of your mana.

**Master of Elements** (levels 51-53) refunds 30% of a spell's base cost on each Fire or Frost crit, which **Shatter** makes common; **Critical Mass** (56-60) adds 10% crit chance to your Fire spells.
caveats: This build takes neither **Heating Up** nor **Pyroblast**, and the tuned rules never cast **Pyroblast** with this list.

The signature rule: the Frostfire spec must do at least 30% of its damage with **Frostfire Bolt**. Two tuned rules serve that floor: **Ice Lance** only above 30% of your mana, and the narrow **Fire Blast** window. They keep the bolt at about 30% and cost a little time: the fight lab measured the whole rule set 0.4% slower per kill than the plain list.
**Cone of Cold** stays out of single pulls (the tuned rules never cast it); **Improved Blizzard**, **Improved Cone of Cold** and **Improved Fire Ward** do nothing on single pulls.
Mana: **Frostfire Bolt** costs 370 at top rank. Drink below a third of your mana and use **Evocation** between fights when it is ready and you are under 40% mana.
Level 40 is the slow spot: about 44 seconds per kill in the fight lab, against 33 at level 30 and 35 at level 50.
diverge: On a nearly dead mob (below a tenth of its health), start no bolt: an **Ice Lance** that will kill, or the wand.
Mob on you with **Frost Nova** down: keep casting the bolt (**Burning Soul** sometimes keeps a hit from pushing it back); **Fire Blast** only inside its window.
